newsitem.title: UK: UK's Offer not consulted over windfall tax.
newsitem.headline: UK's Offer not consulted over windfall tax.

text.p: Stephen Littlechild, Director General of UK electricity regulator Offer, has not been consulted yet by the government over the introduction of a Windfall Tax on profits made by privatised utilities, but expects to be asked for advice soon.

"We have been approached for information," he said, adding this was typically for information about accounting, profit and loss and other cash information, "but we have not been formally asked for a view or consulted by the government."
He said that the Chancellor of the Exchequer, Gordon Brown, has said he would do so, and Littlechild expected to hear from him before the budget on July 2.
He added that Offer did not yet know at what level it would be set, which companies it would be levied on, or on what basis it would be calculated.
Littlechild said he believed that if companies had concerns over the tax, "it will be for the companies to debate with the government rather than with me."
He said that any windfall tax should apply only to a company's past profits and so should not have a bearing on customers, so there should be no need to change existing price controls.
